framework.name: India Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025
framework.version: Act No. 22 of 2023; Rules notified 13-14 November 2025
framework.publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

summary: The obligations of a Data Fiduciary under India's DPDP Act and Rules, and where Hawk AI supports them: security safeguards under Rule 6 (encryption and masking, access control, logs kept a year, backups), breach intimation, erasure, and checks on the AI software a Significant Data Fiduciary uses.
scope: Section and rule numbers of the Act and the Rules; titles are our own short wording. Hawk AI runs on the customer's server and holds personal data of the customer's staff (accounts, activity) and finds personal data in AI traffic. Most obligations apply about 18 months after the Rules were notified (from May 2027); the Board's provisions apply at once.

sources.title: MeitY: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules 2025
DPDP Rules 2025, Rule 6 (reasonable security safeguards), clauses (a)-(g)

notes.title: When it applies
notes.text: Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 (the Board) applied from notification; Rule 4 (consent managers) after 12 months; the Fiduciary's obligations (Rules 3, 5-16, 22, 23) about 18 months after notification, in May 2027.

notes.title: CERT-In directions (28 April 2022)
notes.text: Separate from DPDP: report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours, keep ICT logs 180 days in India and synchronise clocks. These are on the DESC / CERT-In pack and in the incident report.

requirements.title: Process personal data only for a lawful purpose, with consent or for a legitimate use
Give a clear, itemised notice when asking for consent
requirements.note: For Hawk AI's own users, the sign-in notice can say AI use is monitored; notices to customers' own data principals are the customer's.

requirements.title: Consent that is free, specific, informed and can be withdrawn as easily as given
Rely on a legitimate use only where the Act lists one
Stay responsible for processing done by Data Processors
requirements.note: Hawk AI processes on the customer's own server; nothing is sent to the vendor.

requirements.title: Keep personal data complete and accurate when it drives a decision
Put in place technical and organisational measures to comply
Protect personal data with reasonable security safeguards
Encrypt, obfuscate, mask or tokenise personal data
requirements.note: DLP redacts personal identifiers before prompts reach an AI service.

requirements.title: Control access to the computer systems that process it
Log, monitor and review access to detect and investigate misuse
Keep processing going if data is lost or destroyed (backups)
Keep logs and personal data a year to detect and investigate breaches
Put security safeguards in contracts with Data Processors
Make sure the safeguards are actually followed
Tell the Board and each affected person of a breach (full report to the Board within 72 hours)
Erase personal data once its purpose is served, unless a law requires keeping it
Publish who answers questions about the processing
Run an effective way to handle grievances
Verifiable parental consent for children; no tracking or targeted ads at them
Significant Data Fiduciary: yearly impact assessment and audit
Significant Data Fiduciary: check that algorithmic software it uses does not risk people's rights
Significant Data Fiduciary: keep specified data in India where required
Give a person a summary of their personal data and its processing on request
Correct, complete, update or erase a person's data on request
Answer grievances within the period the Rules set
Let a person nominate someone to act for them
Transfer outside India only as the Government allows
